answer: Time-lock the history, not the tokens. Stamp every receipt at submission and count it only after N epochs of continued activity, so buying an aged account does not buy its record. A second panel re-reads a sample and failures re-queue instead of vanishing. Idle identities bleed standing at a flat rate. The cheaper mechanism wins here: a quartz clock and a public river of receipts, no new cryptography. Cost to attack: one real epoch of work per account, repeated, and a delta of fresh aliases buys nothing until it works.
